question: Which of these Nobel Prize-winning authors did NOT win the Pulitzer Prize?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gabriel Garcia Marquez**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gabriel Garcia Marquez**, a Colombian author renowned for his literary works, won the **Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982** for his contributions to the field of magical realism. However, he did not win the **Pulitzer Prize**, which is primarily awarded to American authors or works.
 
• The **Pulitzer Prize** is a prestigious award given in the United States for achievements in journalism, literature, and music. It generally focuses on works written in English or by American authors. *Hence, Gabriel Garcia Marquez did not qualify for this prize.*
 
• **Ernest Hemingway**, another literary giant, won both the **Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954** and the **Pulitzer Prize in 1953** for his novel *The Old Man and the Sea*. *Hence, he is not the correct answer.*
 
• **William Faulkner** also received both accolades. He won the **Nobel Prize in Literature in 1949** and the Pulitzer Prize twice for his works *A Fable* (1955) and *The Reivers* (1963). *Hence, he is not the correct answer.*
 
• **John Steinbeck**, the author of the classic novel *The Grapes of Wrath*, won the **Nobel Prize in Literature in 1962** and the **Pulitzer Prize in 1940** for the same novel. *Hence, he is not the correct answer.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Gabriel Garcia Marquez.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gabriel Garcia Marquez:**

 
 
• **Gabriel Garcia Marquez** is best known for his masterpiece *One Hundred Years of Solitude*, which is a hallmark of the magical realism genre.
 
• He was a Colombian author whose works explored themes of history, culture, and identity in Latin America.
 
• His works, though globally acclaimed, did not fit the criteria for the Pulitzer Prize, which primarily recognizes American contributions.
 
 
 
• **Pulitzer Prize:**
 
 
• The Pulitzer Prize was established in **1917** by provisions in the will of **Joseph Pulitzer**, a Hungarian-American journalist and newspaper publisher.
 
• It is awarded annually in 21 categories, including **fiction, drama, history, and journalism**.
 
 
 
• **Other Authors:**
 
 
• **Ernest Hemingway:** His works are known for their economy and understatement. Notable works include *The Old Man and the Sea* and *A Farewell to Arms*.
 
• **William Faulkner:** Known for his intricate narrative style and exploration of the Southern Gothic tradition. Famous works include *The Sound and the Fury* and *As I Lay Dying*.
 
• **John Steinbeck:** He explored themes of social injustice and the human condition. His notable works include *The Grapes of Wrath* and *Of Mice and Men*.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nobel Prize:**

 
 
• The **Nobel Prize in Literature** is a global recognition awarded annually to authors, poets, and playwrights for their outstanding contributions to the literary world.
 
• This prize has a broader scope than the Pulitzer, as it is not restricted by language or nationality.
 
 
 
• **Key Differences Between the Pulitzer and Nobel Prizes:**
 
 
• **Pulitzer:** Focuses on American achievements and works in English.
 
• **Nobel:** Recognizes global literary contributions, irrespective of language or nationality.
